import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Category.Basic

/-!
# Category Definition (Stacks Tag 0013)

A category C consists of:
1. A collection of objects Ob(C)
2. For each pair x, y ∈ Ob(C), a set of morphisms Mor(x, y)
3. For each object x, an identity morphism id_x ∈ Mor(x, x)
4. Composition: Mor(x, y) × Mor(y, z) → Mor(x, z)

Satisfying associativity and identity laws.

In Mathlib, this is `CategoryTheory.Category`.
-/

namespace StacksProject

-- We use Mathlib's Category which matches Stacks 0013
-- The key components are:
-- * Objects: Type u (the type C itself)
-- * Morphisms: C → C → Type v (written X ⟶ Y)
-- * Identity: 𝟙 X : X ⟶ X
-- * Composition: f ≫ g for f : X ⟶ Y, g : Y ⟶ Z
-- Note: Mathlib uses diagrammatic order (f ≫ g means "f then g")

example {C : Type*} [CategoryTheory.Category C] (X : C) : X ⟶ X := 𝟙 X

example {C : Type*} [CategoryTheory.Category C] {X Y Z : C} 
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z) : X ⟶ Z := f ≫ g

-- Associativity (Stacks: (h ∘ g) ∘ f = h ∘ (g ∘ f))
-- In diagrammatic order: (f ≫ g) ≫ h = f ≫ (g ≫ h)
example {C : Type*} [CategoryTheory.Category C] {W X Y Z : C}
    (f : W ⟶ X) (g : X ⟶ Y) (h : Y ⟶ Z) : (f ≫ g) ≫ h = f ≫ (g ≫ h) :=
  CategoryTheory.Category.assoc f g h

-- Identity laws (Stacks: f ∘ id_x = f = id_y ∘ f)
-- In diagrammatic order: 𝟙 X ≫ f = f and f ≫ 𝟙 Y = f
example {C : Type*} [CategoryTheory.Category C] {X Y : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) : 
    𝟙 X ≫ f = f := CategoryTheory.Category.id_comp f

example {C : Type*} [CategoryTheory.Category C] {X Y : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) : 
    f ≫ 𝟙 Y = f := CategoryTheory.Category.comp_id f

end StacksProject

import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Functor.Basic

/-!
# Functor Definition (Stacks Tag 0014)

A functor F : C → D consists of:
1. A map F : Ob(C) → Ob(D)
2. For each x, y ∈ Ob(C), a map F : Mor(x, y) → Mor(F(x), F(y))

Satisfying:
- F(id_x) = id_{F(x)}
- F(g ∘ f) = F(g) ∘ F(f)
-/

namespace StacksProject

open CategoryTheory

-- Mathlib's Functor matches Stacks 0014
-- * F.obj : C → D (action on objects)
-- * F.map : (X ⟶ Y) → (F.obj X ⟶ F.obj Y) (action on morphisms)

-- Identity preservation: F(id_x) = id_{F(x)}
example {C D : Type*} [Category C] [Category D] (F : C ⥤ D) (X : C) :
    F.map (𝟙 X) = 𝟙 (F.obj X) := F.map_id X

-- Composition preservation: F(g ∘ f) = F(g) ∘ F(f)
-- In diagrammatic order: F.map (f ≫ g) = F.map f ≫ F.map g
example {C D : Type*} [Category C] [Category D] (F : C ⥤ D) 
    {X Y Z : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z) :
    F.map (f ≫ g) = F.map f ≫ F.map g := F.map_comp f g

-- The identity functor
example (C : Type*) [Category C] : C ⥤ C := Functor.id C

-- Functor composition
example {C D E : Type*} [Category C] [Category D] [Category E] 
    (F : C ⥤ D) (G : D ⥤ E) : C ⥤ E := F ⋙ G

end StacksProject

import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.NatTrans

/-!
# Natural Transformation Definition (Stacks Tag 0015)

A natural transformation t : F → G between functors F, G : C → D consists of:
For each x ∈ Ob(C), a morphism t_x : F(x) → G(x)

Naturality: For f : x → y, G(f) ∘ t_x = t_y ∘ F(f)

    F(x) --F(f)--> F(y)
      |             |
     t_x           t_y
      v             v
    G(x) --G(f)--> G(y)
-/

namespace StacksProject

open CategoryTheory

-- Mathlib's NatTrans matches Stacks 0015
-- * τ.app X : F.obj X ⟶ G.obj X (component at X)
-- * τ.naturality : naturality condition

-- The naturality square (in diagrammatic order):
-- F.map f ≫ τ.app Y = τ.app X ≫ G.map f
example {C D : Type*} [Category C] [Category D] 
    {F G : C ⥤ D} (τ : F ⟶ G) {X Y : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) :
    F.map f ≫ τ.app Y = τ.app X ≫ G.map f := τ.naturality f

-- Natural transformations can be composed vertically
example {C D : Type*} [Category C] [Category D] 
    {F G H : C ⥤ D} (τ : F ⟶ G) (σ : G ⟶ H) : F ⟶ H := τ ≫ σ

-- The identity natural transformation
example {C D : Type*} [Category C] [Category D] (F : C ⥤ D) : F ⟶ F := 𝟙 F

-- Natural isomorphism (when all components are isomorphisms)
example {C D : Type*} [Category C] [Category D] 
    {F G : C ⥤ D} (τ : F ≅ G) : F ⟶ G := τ.hom

end StacksProject

import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Opposites

/-!
# Opposite Category Definition (Stacks Tag 0017)

For a category C, the opposite category C^op has:
- Same objects: Ob(C^op) = Ob(C)
- Reversed morphisms: Mor_{C^op}(x, y) = Mor_C(y, x)
- Reversed composition: g ∘^{op} f = f ∘ g
-/

namespace StacksProject

open CategoryTheory

-- Cᵒᵖ is the opposite category
-- Objects are wrapped: Opposite.op X : Cᵒᵖ for X : C
-- We can unwrap: (Opposite.op X).unop = X

example {C : Type*} [Category C] : Category Cᵒᵖ := inferInstance

-- Objects of Cᵒᵖ correspond to objects of C
example {C : Type*} [Category C] (X : C) : Cᵒᵖ := Opposite.op X
example {C : Type*} [Category C] (X : Cᵒᵖ) : C := X.unop

-- Morphisms are reversed: (op X ⟶ op Y) corresponds to (Y ⟶ X)
example {C : Type*} [Category C] {X Y : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) : 
    Opposite.op Y ⟶ Opposite.op X := f.op

example {C : Type*} [Category C] {X Y : Cᵒᵖ} (f : X ⟶ Y) : 
    Y.unop ⟶ X.unop := f.unop

-- Composition is reversed
-- If f : X ⟶ Y and g : Y ⟶ Z in C, then in Cᵒᵖ:
-- g.op : op Z ⟶ op Y and f.op : op Y ⟶ op X
-- g.op ≫ f.op = (f ≫ g).op
example {C : Type*} [Category C] {X Y Z : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z) :
    g.op ≫ f.op = (f ≫ g).op := rfl

-- Double opposite is isomorphic to original
example (C : Type*) [Category C] : (Cᵒᵖ)ᵒᵖ ≌ C := opOpEquivalence C

end StacksProject

statements.informal: Definition of categorical product following Stacks Project Tag 001D
statements.lean_statement:
import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Limits.Shapes.Products
import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Limits.Shapes.BinaryProducts

/-!
# Product Definition (Stacks Tag 001D)

A product of objects x, y in category C is an object x × y with
projections p : x × y → x and q : x × y → y satisfying:

Universal property: For any z with f : z → x and g : z → y,
there exists UNIQUE h : z → x × y such that p ∘ h = f and q ∘ h = g.
-/

namespace StacksProject

open CategoryTheory CategoryTheory.Limits

-- Binary products in Mathlib
variable {C : Type*} [Category C] 

-- A category has binary products if all pairs have a product
example [HasBinaryProducts C] (X Y : C) : C := X ⨯ Y

-- The projections
example [HasBinaryProducts C] (X Y : C) : X ⨯ Y ⟶ X := prod.fst
example [HasBinaryProducts C] (X Y : C) : X ⨯ Y ⟶ Y := prod.snd

-- The universal property: given f : Z ⟶ X and g : Z ⟶ Y, get h : Z ⟶ X ⨯ Y
example [HasBinaryProducts C] {X Y Z : C} (f : Z ⟶ X) (g : Z ⟶ Y) : 
    Z ⟶ X ⨯ Y := prod.lift f g

-- The lift satisfies the universal property
example [HasBinaryProducts C] {X Y Z : C} (f : Z ⟶ X) (g : Z ⟶ Y) :
    prod.lift f g ≫ prod.fst = f := prod.lift_fst f g

example [HasBinaryProducts C] {X Y Z : C} (f : Z ⟶ X) (g : Z ⟶ Y) :
    prod.lift f g ≫ prod.snd = g := prod.lift_snd f g

-- Uniqueness: any morphism satisfying these equations equals the lift
example [HasBinaryProducts C] {X Y Z : C} (f : Z ⟶ X) (g : Z ⟶ Y) 
    (h : Z ⟶ X ⨯ Y) (hf : h ≫ prod.fst = f) (hg : h ≫ prod.snd = g) :
    h = prod.lift f g := prod.hom_ext hf hg

end StacksProject

statements.lean_statement:
import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Limits.Shapes.Pullbacks

/-!
# Fibre Product (Pullback) Definition (Stacks Tag 001K)

Given f : x → z and g : y → z, the fibre product x ×_z y is an object with
p : x ×_z y → x and q : x ×_z y → y such that f ∘ p = g ∘ q, satisfying:

Universal property: For any w with a : w → x, b : w → y where f ∘ a = g ∘ b,
there exists UNIQUE h : w → x ×_z y making everything commute.

      w
     /|\
    a | b
   /  |  \
  v   v   v
  x ×_z y
  |     |
  p     q
  v     v
  x --> z <-- y
     f     g
-/

namespace StacksProject

open CategoryTheory CategoryTheory.Limits

variable {C : Type*} [Category C]

-- Pullbacks in Mathlib
-- Given f : X ⟶ Z and g : Y ⟶ Z, the pullback is written pullback f g

example [HasPullbacks C] {X Y Z : C} (f : X ⟶ Z) (g : Y ⟶ Z) : C := 
  pullback f g

-- The projections
example [HasPullbacks C] {X Y Z : C} (f : X ⟶ Z) (g : Y ⟶ Z) : 
    pullback f g ⟶ X := pullback.fst

example [HasPullbacks C] {X Y Z : C} (f : X ⟶ Z) (g : Y ⟶ Z) : 
    pullback f g ⟶ Y := pullback.snd

-- The pullback condition: f ∘ p = g ∘ q
example [HasPullbacks C] {X Y Z : C} (f : X ⟶ Z) (g : Y ⟶ Z) :
    pullback.fst ≫ f = pullback.snd ≫ g := pullback.condition

-- Universal property: given compatible maps, get the unique lift
example [HasPullbacks C] {W X Y Z : C} (f : X ⟶ Z) (g : Y ⟶ Z)
    (a : W ⟶ X) (b : W ⟶ Y) (h : a ≫ f = b ≫ g) : 
    W ⟶ pullback f g := pullback.lift a b h

-- The lift commutes with projections
example [HasPullbacks C] {W X Y Z : C} (f : X ⟶ Z) (g : Y ⟶ Z)
    (a : W ⟶ X) (b : W ⟶ Y) (h : a ≫ f = b ≫ g) :
    pullback.lift a b h ≫ pullback.fst = a := pullback.lift_fst a b h

example [HasPullbacks C] {W X Y Z : C} (f : X ⟶ Z) (g : Y ⟶ Z)
    (a : W ⟶ X) (b : W ⟶ Y) (h : a ≫ f = b ≫ g) :
    pullback.lift a b h ≫ pullback.snd = b := pullback.lift_snd a b h

-- Uniqueness
example [HasPullbacks C] {W X Y Z : C} (f : X ⟶ Z) (g : Y ⟶ Z)
    (a : W ⟶ X) (b : W ⟶ Y) (h : a ≫ f = b ≫ g)
    (t : W ⟶ pullback f g) (ht1 : t ≫ pullback.fst = a) (ht2 : t ≫ pullback.snd = b) :
    t = pullback.lift a b h := pullback.hom_ext ht1 ht2

end StacksProject

import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Yoneda

/-!
# Representable Functors and Yoneda Embedding

Preparation for Yoneda Lemma (Tag 0019) and Yoneda Embedding (Tag 001P).

For x ∈ Ob(C), the representable functor h_x = Hom(-, x) : C^op → Set
sends each object y to Mor(y, x).
-/

namespace StacksProject

open CategoryTheory

variable {C : Type*} [Category C]

-- The Yoneda embedding: C → (Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type)
-- Sends X to the functor Hom(-, X)
#check @yoneda
-- yoneda : C ⥤ (Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v)

-- For object X, yoneda.obj X is the functor Hom(-, X)
example (X : C) : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type _ := yoneda.obj X

-- On objects: (yoneda.obj X).obj (op Y) = (Y ⟶ X)
example (X Y : C) : (yoneda.obj X).obj (Opposite.op Y) = (Y ⟶ X) := rfl

-- The contravariant Hom functor
example (X : C) : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type _ := yoneda.obj X

-- A functor F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type is representable if it's isomorphic to some h_X
#check @CategoryTheory.Functor.Representable

-- The coyoneda embedding: Cᵒᵖ → (C ⥤ Type)
-- Sends X to the functor Hom(X, -)
#check @coyoneda

end StacksProject

statements.informal: The Yoneda Lemma - natural bijection between natural transformations from representable functors and elements of the target functor
statements.lean_statement:
import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Yoneda

/-!
# Yoneda Lemma (Stacks Tag 0019)

THEOREM: Let C be a category, F : C^op → Type a functor, X ∈ Ob(C).
There is a natural bijection:

    Nat(h_X, F) ≅ F(X)

where h_X = Hom(−, X) is the representable functor (yoneda.obj X).

The bijection sends t ↦ t_X(id_X).
-/

namespace StacksProject

open CategoryTheory

universe v u

variable {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C]

-- The Yoneda lemma in Mathlib: natural isomorphism between
-- Hom(yoneda.obj X, F) and F.obj (op X)
#check @yonedaEquiv
-- yonedaEquiv : (yoneda.obj X ⟶ F) ≃ F.obj (op X)

-- For any functor F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type and object X,
-- natural transformations yoneda.obj X ⟶ F correspond bijectively to F.obj (op X)
example (F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v) (X : C) : 
    (yoneda.obj X ⟶ F) ≃ F.obj (Opposite.op X) := yonedaEquiv

-- The forward direction: given a natural transformation, evaluate at X on id
-- This is exactly t ↦ t_X(id_X) from Stacks
example (F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v) (X : C) (t : yoneda.obj X ⟶ F) :
    F.obj (Opposite.op X) := yonedaEquiv t

-- Explicitly, this is t.app (op X) (𝟙 X)
theorem yoneda_forward_explicit (F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v) (X : C) (t : yoneda.obj X ⟶ F) :
    yonedaEquiv t = t.app (Opposite.op X) (𝟙 X) := by
  simp [yonedaEquiv]

-- The inverse: given an element a ∈ F(X), construct the natural transformation
-- At object Y, it sends f : Y ⟶ X to F(f)(a)
example (F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v) (X : C) (a : F.obj (Opposite.op X)) :
    yoneda.obj X ⟶ F := yonedaEquiv.symm a

-- The equivalence is natural in both X and F
#check @yonedaEquiv_naturality

-- Key computation: the equivalence evaluated
theorem yoneda_computation (F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v) (X : C) 
    (a : F.obj (Opposite.op X)) (Y : Cᵒᵖ) (f : Y.unop ⟶ X) :
    (yonedaEquiv.symm a).app Y f = F.map f.op a := by
  simp [yonedaEquiv]

end StacksProject

statements.informal: The Yoneda embedding is fully faithful - Lemma 4.3.5 of Stacks
statements.lean_statement:
import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Yoneda

/-!
# Yoneda Embedding Fully Faithful (Stacks Tag 001P)

LEMMA 4.3.5: The Yoneda embedding h : C → Fun(C^op, Type) is fully faithful.

This means: Mor_C(X, Y) ≅ Nat(h_X, h_Y)

Equivalently, for any natural transformation s : h_X → h_Y, there is a UNIQUE
morphism φ : X → Y such that h(φ) = s.
-/

namespace StacksProject

open CategoryTheory

universe v u

variable {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C]

-- The Yoneda embedding is full
#check @Yoneda.yoneda_full
-- instance : (yoneda : C ⥤ Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v).Full

-- The Yoneda embedding is faithful
#check @Yoneda.yoneda_faithful
-- instance : (yoneda : C ⥤ Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v).Faithful

-- Combined: fully faithful
example : (yoneda : C ⥤ Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v).FullyFaithful := Yoneda.fullyFaithful

-- What this means concretely:
-- The map yoneda.map : (X ⟶ Y) → (yoneda.obj X ⟶ yoneda.obj Y) is a bijection

-- From a morphism to a natural transformation
example (X Y : C) (f : X ⟶ Y) : yoneda.obj X ⟶ yoneda.obj Y := yoneda.map f

-- The equivalence between morphisms and natural transformations
example (X Y : C) : (X ⟶ Y) ≃ (yoneda.obj X ⟶ yoneda.obj Y) := 
  Yoneda.fullyFaithful.homEquiv

-- Injectivity (faithfulness): if yoneda.map f = yoneda.map g, then f = g
theorem yoneda_injective {X Y : C} {f g : X ⟶ Y} 
    (h : yoneda.map f = yoneda.map g) : f = g := by
  have := Yoneda.fullyFaithful.map_injective h
  exact this

-- Surjectivity (fullness): every natural transformation comes from a morphism
theorem yoneda_surjective {X Y : C} (t : yoneda.obj X ⟶ yoneda.obj Y) :
    ∃ f : X ⟶ Y, yoneda.map f = t := by
  use Yoneda.fullyFaithful.preimage t
  exact Yoneda.fullyFaithful.map_preimage t

-- The inverse: extracting a morphism from a natural transformation
-- This is exactly t_X(id_X) by Yoneda lemma
example (X Y : C) (t : yoneda.obj X ⟶ yoneda.obj Y) : X ⟶ Y := 
  Yoneda.fullyFaithful.preimage t

-- Corollary: Objects are isomorphic iff their representable functors are
theorem yoneda_reflects_iso {X Y : C} :
    (yoneda.obj X ≅ yoneda.obj Y) ≃ (X ≅ Y) := by
  exact Yoneda.fullyFaithful.isoEquiv

end StacksProject

statements.informal: Strategy for proving Stacks 001Z - representability stable under base change
statements.lean_statement:
import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Limits.Shapes.Pullbacks
import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Yoneda

/-!
# Strategy for Pullback Stability (Stacks Tag 001Z)

LEMMA 4.6.6: Representability is stable under base change.

If f : X → Y is representable and y' → Y is any morphism, then the
pullback X' = X ×_Y Y' → Y' is also representable.

NOTE: This requires understanding what "representable morphism" means
in the context of the Stacks project, which involves fibered categories
or the functor-of-points perspective.
-/

namespace StacksProject

open CategoryTheory CategoryTheory.Limits

/-
Key insight: In the Stacks Project, "representable" for a morphism of functors
or a morphism in a category often means that certain fiber products exist
and have a specific form.

For a morphism f : F → G of presheaves (functors C^op → Set), f is representable
if for every representable G' → G, the fiber product F ×_G G' is representable.

The lemma says: if we know f : X → Y is representable, and we base change
along any Y' → Y, then X' = X ×_Y Y' → Y' is also representable.

In Mathlib, this relates to:
- Representable morphisms of presheaves
- Pullback squares preserve representability
-/

-- Pullback pasting lemma: useful for the proof
#check @pullbackSymmetry
#check @pullbackAssoc

-- For presheaves specifically, see:
-- Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Functor.Representable

/-
PROOF STRATEGY for Tag 001Z:

1. Interpret "representable morphism" - in functor-of-points view, 
   f : F → G is representable if for all X and α : h_X → G,
   the pullback F ×_G h_X is representable.

2. Given f : X → Y representable and g : Y' → Y, need to show X ×_Y Y' → Y'
   is representable.

3. For any test object Z with β : h_Z → Y', compute:
   (X ×_Y Y') ×_{Y'} h_Z ≅ X ×_Y (Y' ×_{Y'} h_Z) ≅ X ×_Y h_Z
   (using pullback pasting/associativity)

4. Since f : X → Y is representable, X ×_Y h_Z is representable.

This would require setting up the presheaf perspective properly.
-/

end StacksProject

statements.name: RepresentableMap
statements.informal:
|
  Define “representable morphism” in a category with pullbacks, in the sense used in Stacks Tag 001Z:
  a morphism f : X ⟶ Y is representable if for every base change g : Y' ⟶ Y,
  the pullback X ×_Y Y' exists and is representable as an object (i.e. isomorphic
  to some object of the category). In pure category theory, “representable as an
  object” is tautological; in the Stacks context this is meant relative to a larger
  ambient category (e.g. sheaves), so we package the minimal base-change predicate
  that later can be refined to the geometric setting.
statements.lean_statement:
import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Limits.Shapes.Pullbacks

  namespace Stacks

  open CategoryTheory
  open CategoryTheory.Limits

  universe v u

  variable {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C]

  /--
  A minimal “representable morphism” predicate suited for formalizing Stacks 001Z.

  In the Stacks project, representability is usually relative to a functor
  `C ⥤ D` (e.g. schemes inside sheaves), and the definition says every base change
  stays inside the smaller subcategory. Pure category theory does not see that.

  This definition is therefore intentionally *skeletal*: it expresses the
  base-change stability condition one would need to prove, and it is parameterized
  only by existence of pullbacks. In later phases, refine this to a relative notion.
  -/
  def RepresentableMap (f : X ⟶ Y) : Prop :=
    ∀ ⦃Y' : C⦄ (g : Y' ⟶ Y), Nonempty (IsLimit (pullbackCone f g))

end Stacks

statements.name: RepresentableMap
statements.informal:
|
  Formal base-change stability statement in the minimal setting: if a map is
  “representable” (in the sense that all pullbacks exist), then any base change
  of it is again representable.
statements.lean_statement:
import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Limits.Shapes.Pullbacks

namespace Stacks

open CategoryTheory
open CategoryTheory.Limits

universe v u

variable {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C]

def RepresentableMap {X Y : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) : Prop :=
  ∀ ⦃Y' : C⦄ (g : Y' ⟶ Y), Nonempty (IsLimit (pullbackCone f g))

/--
Minimal “representability is stable under base change”: if all pullbacks of `f` exist,
then all pullbacks of the base-changed morphism `pullback.snd : pullback f g ⟶ Y'` exist.

This matches the formal skeleton of Stacks 001Z, but does not yet incorporate a
subcategory/ambient category distinction.
-/
theorem representableMap_stable_under_base_change
    {X Y Y' : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y' ⟶ Y)
    (hf : RepresentableMap f) :
    RepresentableMap (pullback.snd f g) := by
  intro Y'' k
  -- We need a pullback of (pullback.snd f g) along k : Y'' ⟶ Y'.
  -- Consider the composite Y'' ⟶ Y' ⟶ Y and use hf to get a pullback of f along it.
  rcases hf (g := k ≫ g) with ⟨tlim⟩
  -- Now: pullback of pullback.snd along k can be constructed as an iterated pullback.
  -- Mathlib provides existence via `IsLimit` transfer along isomorphisms of cones.
  -- Easiest: use typeclass-driven construction by turning `tlim` into `[HasPullback f (k ≫ g)]`,
  -- then derive `[HasPullback (pullback.snd f g) k]` using existing lemmas about pullbacks.
  --
  -- We can do this by invoking `hasPullback_of_isLimit` and then `infer_instance`.
  classical
  letI : HasPullback f (k ≫ g) := ⟨⟨_, tlim⟩⟩
  -- With this instance, the needed pullback exists by the fact that pullbacks compose:
  -- `HasPullback (pullback.snd f g) k` is available in Mathlib.
  letI : HasPullback (pullback.snd f g) k := by infer_instance
  -- Package the typeclass pullback as `Nonempty (IsLimit (pullbackCone ...))`.
  refine ⟨?_⟩
  exact (pullbackIsPullback (pullback.snd f g) k)

  relative to a functor/subcategory, and stability under base change as closure under pullbacks
  in the ambient category.
statements.lean_statement:
/-
Future direction (not code):

In geometry, one often has:
  i : D ⥤ C  (e.g. Schemes ⥤ Sheaves)
and says: a morphism f : X ⟶ Y in C is representable (by objects of D) if for every
g : i.obj T ⟶ Y (or more generally any g : Y' ⟶ Y), the pullback X ×_Y Y'
is isomorphic to i.obj T' for some T' : D.

In Lean/Mathlib, this can be expressed via:
  ∃ T' : D, Nonempty (pullback f g ≅ i.obj T')
or via essential image:
  pullback f g ∈ Functor.essImage i
(there is a bundled predicate `Functor.essImage`).

Then base change stability is almost tautological:
if for all g we land in essImage i, then for all k we also land in essImage i
by composing k with g and using associativity of pullbacks (or existence of an
isomorphism between iterated pullbacks).

You will likely want:
  - a lemma giving an iso between (pullback (pullback.snd f g) k) and pullback f (k ≫ g)
    (`pullbackAssoc`-style)
  - then transport membership in the essential image across isomorphisms.
-/

statements.name: representingObjectIso
statements.informal: The representing object of a functor is unique up to unique isomorphism (Tag 0020).
statements.lean_statement:
import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Yoneda
import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Functor.FullyFaithful

namespace Stacks

open CategoryTheory

universe v u

variable {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C]

/--
If a presheaf F is represented by both X and Y, then X and Y are isomorphic.
The isomorphism is uniquely determined by the isomorphism of functors.
Stacks Project Tag 0020.
-/
noncomputable def representingObjectIso {F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v} {X Y : C}
    (iX : F ≅ yoneda.obj X) (iY : F ≅ yoneda.obj Y) : X ≅ Y :=
  let i : yoneda.obj X ≅ yoneda.obj Y := iX.symm ≪≫ iY
  Functor.preimageIso i

/--
The isomorphism constructed in `representingObjectIso` induces the original
isomorphism of functors.
-/
lemma representingObjectIso_spec {F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v} {X Y : C}
    (iX : F ≅ yoneda.obj X) (iY : F ≅ yoneda.obj Y) :
    yoneda.map (representingObjectIso iX iY).hom = iX.inv ≫ iY.hom := by
  -- We use the property that the Yoneda embedding is fully faithful.
  -- Functor.map_preimageIso states that mapping the preimage iso gives back the original iso.
  dsimp [representingObjectIso]
  rw [Functor.map_preimageIso]
  rfl

end Stacks

statements.informal: The Yoneda embedding is injective on objects up to isomorphism - if yoneda.obj X ≅ yoneda.obj Y then X ≅ Y
statements.lean_statement:
import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Yoneda

namespace Stacks

open CategoryTheory

universe v u

variable {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C]

/--
The Yoneda embedding reflects isomorphisms on objects:
if the representable functors are isomorphic, so are the representing objects.
This is a consequence of the Yoneda embedding being fully faithful.
-/
theorem yoneda_reflects_iso (X Y : C) (h : yoneda.obj X ≅ yoneda.obj Y) : X ≅ Y :=
  (yoneda.objObjPreimageIso h.hom).symm

/--
Alternative formulation: extracting the isomorphism via the fully faithful property.
Since yoneda is fully faithful, we can preimage any iso between yoneda.obj X and yoneda.obj Y.
-/
theorem yoneda_reflects_iso' (X Y : C) (h : yoneda.obj X ≅ yoneda.obj Y) : X ≅ Y :=
  Functor.preimageIso yoneda h

end Stacks

statements.name: natTrans_comp_assoc
statements.informal: Vertical composition of natural transformations - foundational for functor categories
statements.lean_statement:
import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.NatTrans

namespace Stacks

open CategoryTheory

universe v₁ v₂ u₁ u₂

variable {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁} C]
variable {D : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂} D]

/--
Vertical composition of natural transformations is associative.
Given F, G, H, K : C ⥤ D and α : F ⟶ G, β : G ⟶ H, γ : H ⟶ K,
we have (γ ≫ β) ≫ α = γ ≫ (β ≫ α).
-/
theorem natTrans_comp_assoc {F G H K : C ⥤ D} 
    (α : F ⟶ G) (β : G ⟶ H) (γ : H ⟶ K) :
    α ≫ β ≫ γ = (α ≫ β) ≫ γ := by
  rfl  -- This is definitional in Mathlib due to how ≫ is defined

/--
The identity natural transformation acts as identity for composition.
-/
theorem natTrans_id_comp {F G : C ⥤ D} (α : F ⟶ G) :
    𝟙 F ≫ α = α := by
  simp

theorem natTrans_comp_id {F G : C ⥤ D} (α : F ⟶ G) :
    α ≫ 𝟙 G = α := by
  simp

/--
Naturality square commutes: for any f : X ⟶ Y and natural transformation α : F ⟶ G,
we have α.app Y ≫ F.map f = G.map f ≫ α.app X (in diagrammatic order).
This is the naturality condition restated.
-/
theorem naturality_square {F G : C ⥤ D} (α : F ⟶ G) {X Y : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) :
    F.map f ≫ α.app Y = α.app X ≫ G.map f :=
  α.naturality f

end Stacks

import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Opposites

namespace Stacks

open CategoryTheory

universe v u

variable (C : Type u) [Category.{v} C]

/--
The double opposite of an object is the original object (definitionally in Mathlib's setup).
-/
example (X : C) : (Opposite.op (Opposite.op X)).unop.unop = X := rfl

/--
There is a canonical equivalence between C and (Cᵒᵖ)ᵒᵖ.
-/
def opOpEquiv : C ≌ (Cᵒᵖ)ᵒᵖ := opOpEquivalence C

/--
The functor from C to (Cᵒᵖ)ᵒᵖ sends X to op(op(X)).
-/
theorem opOpEquiv_obj (X : C) : 
    (opOpEquiv C).functor.obj X = Opposite.op (Opposite.op X) := rfl

The double op of a morphism: given f : X ⟶ Y in C,
f.op.op : op(op(X)) ⟶ op(op(Y)) in (Cᵒᵖ)ᵒᵖ
-/
theorem opOpEquiv_map {X Y : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) :
    (opOpEquiv C).functor.map f = f.op.op := rfl

end Stacks

statements.name: prodSymm
statements.informal: Binary products are symmetric - X × Y ≅ Y × X
statements.lean_statement:
import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Limits.Shapes.BinaryProducts

namespace Stacks

open CategoryTheory Limits

universe v u

variable {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] [HasBinaryProducts C]

/--
Binary products are symmetric: X × Y ≅ Y × X.
The isomorphism is given by the universal property.
-/
def prodSymm (X Y : C) : X ⨯ Y ≅ Y ⨯ X :=
  prod.braiding X Y

/--
The symmetry isomorphism swaps the projections.
-/
theorem prodSymm_fst (X Y : C) : 
    (prodSymm X Y).hom ≫ prod.fst = prod.snd := by
  simp [prodSymm, prod.braiding]

theorem prodSymm_snd (X Y : C) : 
    (prodSymm X Y).hom ≫ prod.snd = prod.fst := by
  simp [prodSymm, prod.braiding]

/--
The symmetry isomorphism is self-inverse.
-/
theorem prodSymm_symm (X Y : C) : 
    (prodSymm X Y).symm = prodSymm Y X := by
  ext
  simp [prodSymm, prod.braiding]

end Stacks

statements.name: pullbackSymmetry
statements.informal: Pullbacks are symmetric - the pullback of f along g is isomorphic to the pullback of g along f
statements.lean_statement:
import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Limits.Shapes.Pullbacks

namespace Stacks

open CategoryTheory Limits

universe v u

variable {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C]

/--
Pullbacks are symmetric: X ×_Z Y ≅ Y ×_Z X.
Given f : X ⟶ Z and g : Y ⟶ Z, the pullback of f along g
is isomorphic to the pullback of g along f.
-/
def pullbackSymmetry {X Y Z : C} (f : X ⟶ Z) (g : Y ⟶ Z) 
    [HasPullback f g] [HasPullback g f] :
    pullback f g ≅ pullback g f :=
  pullbackSymmetry f g

/--
Under the symmetry isomorphism, fst and snd are swapped.
-/
theorem pullbackSymmetry_fst {X Y Z : C} (f : X ⟶ Z) (g : Y ⟶ Z) 
    [HasPullback f g] [HasPullback g f] :
    (pullbackSymmetry f g).hom ≫ pullback.fst = pullback.snd :=
  Limits.pullbackSymmetry_hom_comp_fst f g

theorem pullbackSymmetry_snd {X Y Z : C} (f : X ⟶ Z) (g : Y ⟶ Z) 
    [HasPullback f g] [HasPullback g f] :
    (pullbackSymmetry f g).hom ≫ pullback.snd = pullback.fst :=
  Limits.pullbackSymmetry_hom_comp_snd f g

end Stacks

statements.name: theorem_yoneda_preserves_limits_d04100fa
statements.informal: The Yoneda embedding preserves all limits - representable functors are continuous
statements.lean_statement:
import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Yoneda
import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Limits.Yoneda

namespace Stacks

open CategoryTheory Limits

universe v u

variable {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C]

/--
The Yoneda embedding preserves all limits.
This means: if a diagram in C has a limit, then applying yoneda
to the diagram gives a diagram in the presheaf category whose limit
is yoneda applied to the original limit.

Concretely: Hom(-, lim D) ≅ lim Hom(-, D_i) naturally.
-/
instance : PreservesLimits (yoneda : C ⥤ Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v) :=
  yonedaPreservesLimits

/--
The contravariant Yoneda embedding (coyoneda) preserves colimits,
which dually means it sends limits in C to limits.
-/
instance : PreservesLimits (coyoneda : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ C ⥤ Type v) :=
  coyonedaPreservesLimits

end Stacks

statements.name: yoneda_preserves_limits
statements.informal:
|
  The Yoneda embedding preserves all (small) limits. Concretely, for any diagram `K : J ⥤ C`,
  the canonical comparison map `yoneda.obj (limit K) ⟶ limit (K ⋙ yoneda)` is an isomorphism.
  This packages the slogan “representable functors are continuous” in a way that is directly
  reusable for later limit/pullback arguments.
statements.lean_statement:
import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Yoneda
import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Limits.Yoneda

namespace Stacks

open CategoryTheory
open CategoryTheory.Limits

universe v u uJ

variable {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C]
variable {J : Type uJ} [Category.{v} J]

/--
Yoneda preserves all limits: `yoneda : C ⥤ (Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v)` is a continuous functor.
This is the formal Mathlib statement corresponding to “representable functors preserve limits”.
-/
theorem yoneda_preserves_limits : PreservesLimits (yoneda : C ⥤ (Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v)) := by
  infer_instance

/--
A convenient corollary form: for any diagram `K : J ⥤ C`, the comparison morphism
exhibits `yoneda.obj (limit K)` as the limit of `K ⋙ yoneda`.
-/
theorem yoneda_map_limit_iso (K : J ⥤ C) :
    (yoneda.obj (limit K)) ≅ limit (K ⋙ yoneda) := by
  classical
  -- `PreservesLimit.iso` gives the canonical iso when the limit exists.
  simpa using (PreservesLimit.iso (F := (yoneda : C ⥤ (Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v))) K)

end Stacks

import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.EpiMono
import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Category.Basic

/-!
# Monomorphisms, Epimorphisms, and Isomorphisms (Stacks Tag 0018)

Definitions of special types of morphisms in a category.
-/

namespace Stacks

open CategoryTheory

variable {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C]

/-- 
Tag 0018: A morphism f : x ⟶ y is an epimorphism if for all z and g, h : y ⟶ z,
g ∘ f = h ∘ f implies g = h.
In Mathlib notation (diagrammatic): f ≫ g = f ≫ h → g = h.
-/
abbrev IsEpimorphism {X Y : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) : Prop := Epi f

/--
Tag 0018: A morphism f : x ⟶ y is a monomorphism if for all z and g, h : z ⟶ x,
f ∘ g = f ∘ h implies g = h.
In Mathlib notation: g ≫ f = h ≫ f → g = h.
-/
abbrev IsMonomorphism {X Y : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) : Prop := Mono f

/--
Tag 0018: f is a split monomorphism if there exists g such that g ∘ f = id_x.
In this case g is called a retraction of f.
-/
abbrev IsSplitMonomorphism {X Y : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) : Prop := SplitMono f

/--
Tag 0018: f is a split epimorphism if there exists g such that f ∘ g = id_y.
In this case g is called a section of f.
-/
abbrev IsSplitEpimorphism {X Y : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) : Prop := SplitEpi f

/--
Tag 0018: f is an isomorphism if there exists g such that f ∘ g = id_y and g ∘ f = id_x.
-/
abbrev IsIsomorphism {X Y : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) : Prop := IsIso f

-- Verification of basic properties mentioned in Tag 0018

/-- Composition of monomorphisms is a monomorphism -/
example {X Y Z : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z) [Mono f] [Mono g] : Mono (f ≫ g) := inferInstance

/-- Composition of epimorphisms is an epimorphism -/
example {X Y Z : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z) [Epi f] [Epi g] : Epi (f ≫ g) := inferInstance

/-- An isomorphism is both mono and epi -/
example {X Y : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsIso f] : Mono f := inferInstance
example {X Y : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsIso f] : Epi f := inferInstance

/-- A split monomorphism is a monomorphism -/
example {X Y : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) [SplitMono f] : Mono f := by infer_instance

/-- A split epimorphism is an epimorphism -/
example {X Y : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) [SplitEpi f] : Epi f := by infer_instance

end Stacks

# Initial and Terminal Objects (Stacks Tag 001F)

namespace Stacks

open CategoryTheory CategoryTheory.Limits

variable {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C]

/--
Tag 001F: x is initial if Mor(x, y) is a singleton for all y.
Mathlib: `IsInitial x`

abbrev IsInitialObject (x : C) : Prop := IsInitial x

/--
Tag 001F: x is terminal if Mor(y, x) is a singleton for all y.
Mathlib: `IsTerminal x`
-/
abbrev IsTerminalObject (x : C) : Prop := IsTerminal x

/-- The proposition that C has an initial object -/

/-- The proposition that C has a terminal object -/
abbrev HasTerminal (C : Type u) [Category.{v} C] : Prop := HasTerminal C

  IsInitial.uniqueUpToIso hx hy

noncomputable def terminal_unique (x y : C) (hx : IsTerminalObject x) (hy : IsTerminalObject y) : x ≅ y :=
  IsTerminal.uniqueUpToIso hx hy

statements.informal: Definition of coproducts following Stacks Tag 001E.

import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Limits.Shapes.BinaryProducts

/-!
# Coproduct Definition (Stacks Tag 001E)
-/

namespace Stacks

open CategoryTheory CategoryTheory.Limits

variable {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C]

/--
Tag 001E: Coproduct of x and y.
A coproduct is an object x ⨿ y equipped with maps from x and y,
satisfying the universal property (maps out are pairs of maps).
-/
abbrev HasCoproducts (C : Type u) [Category.{v} C] : Prop := HasBinaryCoproducts C

variable [HasBinaryCoproducts C]

/-- The coproduct object x ⨿ y -/
abbrev coproduct (x y : C) : C := x ⨿ y

/-- The inclusion maps -/
abbrev coproduct.inl {x y : C} : x ⟶ coproduct x y := coprod.inl
abbrev coproduct.inr {x y : C} : y ⟶ coproduct x y := coprod.inr

/-- The universal property map: given f: x -> z, g: y -> z, get x ⨿ y -> z -/
def coproduct.desc {x y z : C} (f : x ⟶ z) (g : y ⟶ z) : coproduct x y ⟶ z :=
  coprod.desc f g

-- Verification of axioms from Tag 001E
example {x y z : C} (f : x ⟶ z) (g : y ⟶ z) :
  coproduct.inl ≫ coproduct.desc f g = f := coprod.inl_desc f g

example {x y z : C} (f : x ⟶ z) (g : y ⟶ z) :
  coproduct.inr ≫ coproduct.desc f g = g := coprod.inr_desc f g

example {x y z : C} (f : x ⟶ z) (g : y ⟶ z) (h : coproduct x y ⟶ z)
  (h1 : coproduct.inl ≫ h = f) (h2 : coproduct.inr ≫ h = g) :
  h = coproduct.desc f g :=
  coprod.hom_ext h1 h2

end Stacks

import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Limits.Shapes.Pushouts

/-!
# Pushout Definition (Stacks Tag 001L)
-/

namespace Stacks

open CategoryTheory CategoryTheory.Limits

variable {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C]

/--
Tag 001L: Pushout of f : z ⟶ x and g : z ⟶ y.
Also called the fibre coproduct or cocartesian square.
-/
abbrev HasPushouts (C : Type u) [Category.{v} C] : Prop := HasPushouts C

variable [HasPushouts C]

/-- The pushout object x ⨿_z y -/
abbrev pushout {x y z : C} (f : z ⟶ x) (g : z ⟶ y) : C := CategoryTheory.Limits.pushout f g

/-- The canonical maps -/
abbrev pushout.inl {x y z : C} {f : z ⟶ x} {g : z ⟶ y} : x ⟶ pushout f g := CategoryTheory.Limits.pushout.inl
abbrev pushout.inr {x y z : C} {f : z ⟶ x} {g : z ⟶ y} : y ⟶ pushout f g := CategoryTheory.Limits.pushout.inr

/-- Commutativity of the square -/
example {x y z : C} {f : z ⟶ x} {g : z ⟶ y} :
  f ≫ pushout.inl = g ≫ pushout.inr := CategoryTheory.Limits.pushout.condition

/-- Universal property: given maps from x and y that agree on z, they factor through the pushout -/
def pushout.desc {x y z w : C} {f : z ⟶ x} {g : z ⟶ y}
  (a : x ⟶ w) (b : y ⟶ w) (h : f ≫ a = g ≫ b) : pushout f g ⟶ w :=
  CategoryTheory.Limits.pushout.desc a b h

end Stacks

statements.informal: Definitions of initial and terminal objects following Stacks Tag 001F - fixed version
statements.lean_statement:
import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Limits.Shapes.Terminal

/-!
# Initial and Terminal Objects (Stacks Tag 001F)

An object x in a category C is:
- Initial: if for every object y, there exists a unique morphism x → y
- Terminal: if for every object y, there exists a unique morphism y → x

In Mathlib, these are captured by `IsInitial` and `IsTerminal` predicates,
and `HasInitial`/`HasTerminal` typeclasses for categories possessing such objects.
-/

namespace Stacks

open CategoryTheory Limits

universe v u

variable {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C]

-- Mathlib's IsInitial captures the Stacks definition
#check @IsInitial
-- IsInitial : C → Prop (essentially)

-- Mathlib's IsTerminal captures the Stacks definition
#check @IsTerminal
-- IsTerminal : C → Prop (essentially)

/-- An initial object has a unique morphism to any other object -/
example (I : C) (hI : IsInitial I) (X : C) : Unique (I ⟶ X) :=
  hI.uniqueUpToIso.symm ▸ IsInitial.uniqueUpToIso hI |>.homFromInitial X |> fun _ => hI.unique

/-- Actually, Mathlib provides this directly -/
example (I : C) (hI : IsInitial I) (X : C) : Unique (I ⟶ X) :=
  IsInitial.uniqueTo hI X

/-- A terminal object has a unique morphism from any other object -/
example (T : C) (hT : IsTerminal T) (X : C) : Unique (X ⟶ T) :=
  IsTerminal.uniqueFrom hT X

/-- Initial objects are unique up to unique isomorphism -/
theorem initial_unique_up_to_iso (I J : C) (hI : IsInitial I) (hJ : IsInitial J) : I ≅ J :=
  hI.uniqueUpToIso hJ

/-- Terminal objects are unique up to unique isomorphism -/
theorem terminal_unique_up_to_iso (T S : C) (hT : IsTerminal T) (hS : IsTerminal S) : T ≅ S :=
  hT.uniqueUpToIso hS

/-- The unique morphism from an initial object -/
def morphismFromInitial (I X : C) (hI : IsInitial I) : I ⟶ X :=
  hI.to X

/-- The unique morphism to a terminal object -/
def morphismToTerminal (X T : C) (hT : IsTerminal T) : X ⟶ T :=
  hT.from X

/-- An initial object is terminal in the opposite category -/
theorem initial_op_is_terminal (I : C) (hI : IsInitial I) : IsTerminal (Opposite.op I) :=
  isTerminalOpOfIsInitial hI

/-- A terminal object is initial in the opposite category -/
theorem terminal_op_is_initial (T : C) (hT : IsTerminal T) : IsInitial (Opposite.op T) :=
  isInitialOpOfIsTerminal hT

end Stacks

/-!
# Equalizer Definition (Stacks Tag 001G)

Given two morphisms f, g : x → y, the equalizer is an object e with
a morphism i : e → x such that f ∘ i = g ∘ i, satisfying the universal property:

For any z with h : z → x such that f ∘ h = g ∘ h,
there exists a unique k : z → e with i ∘ k = h.
-/

namespace Stacks

open CategoryTheory Limits

universe v u

variable {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C]

-- Mathlib's equalizer definition
#check @equalizer
#check @equalizer.ι
#check @equalizer.lift

/-- The equalizer morphism satisfies the fork condition -/
theorem equalizer_condition {X Y : C} (f g : X ⟶ Y) [HasEqualizer f g] :
    equalizer.ι f g ≫ f = equalizer.ι f g ≫ g :=
  equalizer.condition f g

/-- Universal property: lifting to the equalizer -/
theorem equalizer_lift_spec {X Y Z : C} (f g : X ⟶ Y) [HasEqualizer f g]
    (h : Z ⟶ X) (w : h ≫ f = h ≫ g) :
    equalizer.lift h w ≫ equalizer.ι f g = h :=
  equalizer.lift_ι h w

/-- The lift to an equalizer is unique -/
theorem equalizer_lift_unique {X Y Z : C} (f g : X ⟶ Y) [HasEqualizer f g]
    (h : Z ⟶ X) (w : h ≫ f = h ≫ g) (k : Z ⟶ equalizer f g)
    (hk : k ≫ equalizer.ι f g = h) :
    k = equalizer.lift h w :=
  equalizer.hom_ext (by rw [hk, equalizer.lift_ι])

/-- The equalizer map is a monomorphism -/
theorem equalizer_is_mono {X Y : C} (f g : X ⟶ Y) [HasEqualizer f g] :
    Mono (equalizer.ι f g) :=
  inferInstance

/-- Coequalizers are dual to equalizers -/
#check @coequalizer
#check @coequalizer.π

/-- The coequalizer morphism satisfies the cofork condition -/
theorem coequalizer_condition {X Y : C} (f g : X ⟶ Y) [HasCoequalizer f g] :
    f ≫ coequalizer.π f g = g ≫ coequalizer.π f g :=
  coequalizer.condition f g

/-- The coequalizer map is an epimorphism -/
theorem coequalizer_is_epi {X Y : C} (f g : X ⟶ Y) [HasCoequalizer f g] :
    Epi (coequalizer.π f g) :=
  inferInstance

end Stacks

statements.informal: The category of functors between two categories (functor category) - Stacks Tag 001S
statements.lean_statement:
import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Functor.Category

/-!
# Functor Category (Stacks Tag 001S)

Given categories C and D, the functor category Fun(C, D) has:
- Objects: Functors F : C ⥤ D
- Morphisms: Natural transformations between functors
- Composition: Vertical composition of natural transformations
- Identity: The identity natural transformation
-/

namespace Stacks

open CategoryTheory

universe v₁ v₂ u₁ u₂

variable (C : Type u₁) [Category.{v₁} C]
variable (D : Type u₂) [Category.{v₂} D]

-- Mathlib notation: C ⥤ D is the functor category
#check (C ⥤ D)

-- It is indeed a category
example : Category (C ⥤ D) := inferInstance

/-- Objects of the functor category are functors -/
example (F : C ⥤ D) : C ⥤ D := F

/-- Morphisms are natural transformations -/
example (F G : C ⥤ D) : Type _ := F ⟶ G  -- NatTrans F G

/-- Identity natural transformation -/
example (F : C ⥤ D) : F ⟶ F := 𝟙 F

/-- Composition of natural transformations -/
example (F G H : C ⥤ D) (α : F ⟶ G) (β : G ⟶ H) : F ⟶ H := α ≫ β

variable {C D}

/-- Component of a natural transformation -/
theorem nat_trans_component (F G : C ⥤ D) (α : F ⟶ G) (X : C) :
    (α.app X : F.obj X ⟶ G.obj X) = α.app X := rfl

/-- Composition is computed componentwise -/
theorem nat_trans_comp_app (F G H : C ⥤ D) (α : F ⟶ G) (β : G ⟶ H) (X : C) :
    (α ≫ β).app X = α.app X ≫ β.app X := rfl

/-- Identity is identity at each component -/
theorem nat_trans_id_app (F : C ⥤ D) (X : C) :
    (𝟙 F : F ⟶ F).app X = 𝟙 (F.obj X) := rfl

/-- Horizontal composition of natural transformations (whiskering) -/
example (E : Type*) [Category E] (F G : C ⥤ D) (H : D ⥤ E) (α : F ⟶ G) :
    F ⋙ H ⟶ G ⋙ H := whiskerRight α H

example (E : Type*) [Category E] (F : C ⥤ D) (G H : D ⥤ E) (β : G ⟶ H) :
    F ⋙ G ⟶ F ⋙ H := whiskerLeft F β

end Stacks

statements.name: equivalence_fully_faithful
statements.informal: Definition and properties of equivalence of categories - Stacks Tag 001R
statements.lean_statement:
import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Equivalence

/-!
# Equivalence of Categories (Stacks Tag 001R)

An equivalence between categories C and D consists of:
- Functors F : C ⥤ D and G : D ⥤ C
- Natural isomorphisms η : 𝟙 C ≅ F ⋙ G and ε : G ⋙ F ≅ 𝟙 D

A functor is an equivalence iff it is fully faithful and essentially surjective.
-/

namespace Stacks

open CategoryTheory

universe v₁ v₂ u₁ u₂

variable {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁} C]
variable {D : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂} D]

-- Mathlib's Equivalence type
#check Equivalence C D
#check (C ≌ D)  -- notation for Equivalence C D

/-- An equivalence consists of functors and natural isomorphisms -/
example (e : C ≌ D) : C ⥤ D := e.functor
example (e : C ≌ D) : D ⥤ C := e.inverse
example (e : C ≌ D) : 𝟭 C ≅ e.functor ⋙ e.inverse := e.unitIso
example (e : C ≌ D) : e.inverse ⋙ e.functor ≅ 𝟭 D := e.counitIso

/-- A functor that is part of an equivalence is fully faithful -/
theorem equivalence_fully_faithful (e : C ≌ D) : e.functor.FullyFaithful :=
  e.fullyFaithfulFunctor

/-- A functor that is part of an equivalence is essentially surjective -/
theorem equivalence_ess_surj (e : C ≌ D) : e.functor.EssSurj :=
  Equivalence.essSurj_of_equivalence e.functor

/-- Equivalences compose -/
example (e₁ : C ≌ D) {E : Type*} [Category E] (e₂ : D ≌ E) : C ≌ E :=
  e₁.trans e₂

/-- Every equivalence has an inverse equivalence -/
example (e : C ≌ D) : D ≌ C := e.symm

/-- The identity functor gives an equivalence -/
example : C ≌ C := Equivalence.refl

/-- An equivalence preserves and reflects isomorphisms -/
example (e : C ≌ D) {X Y : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsIso f] : IsIso (e.functor.map f) :=
  inferInstance

/-- Equivalences preserve limits -/
example (e : C ≌ D) : e.functor.PreservesLimits :=
  Equivalence.preservesLimits e.functor

/-- Equivalences preserve colimits -/
example (e : C ≌ D) : e.functor.PreservesColimits :=
  Equivalence.preservesColimits e.functor

end Stacks

statements.name: yonedaEquiv_naturality_in_x
statements.informal:
|
  A small but useful add-on to the Yoneda lemma API: spelling out how `yonedaEquiv`
  behaves with respect to postcomposition by a morphism `f : X ⟶ Y`. This is the
  “elementwise” form of naturality in the representing object.
statements.lean_statement:
import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Yoneda

namespace Stacks

open CategoryTheory

universe v u
variable {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C]
variable {F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v}
variable {X Y : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) (τ : yoneda.obj X ⟶ F)

/--
Under the Yoneda equivalence, precomposing a natural transformation
`τ : Hom(-, X) ⟶ F` with `yoneda.map f : Hom(-, X) ⟶ Hom(-, Y)` corresponds to
applying `F.map f.op` to the element of `F.obj (op X)`.

Concretely:
`yonedaEquiv Y F (τ ≫ F?) = F.map f.op (yonedaEquiv X F τ)`.

Mathlib already contains this as `yonedaEquiv_naturality`.
We restate it under a Stacks-facing name.
-/
lemma yonedaEquiv_naturality_in_x :
    (yonedaEquiv Y F) ((yoneda.map f) ≫ τ) =
      F.map f.op ((yonedaEquiv X F) τ) := by
  simpa using (yonedaEquiv_naturality (F := F) (f := f) (τ := τ))

end Stacks

statements.name: yonedaEquiv_apply_id
statements.informal:
|
  Computational form of Yoneda: for `τ : Hom(-, X) ⟶ F`, the element of `F(X)`
  corresponding to `τ` is `τ.app (op X) (𝟙 X)`.
statements.lean_statement:
import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Yoneda

namespace Stacks

open CategoryTheory

universe v u
variable {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C]
variable {F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v}
variable (X : C) (τ : yoneda.obj X ⟶ F)

lemma yonedaEquiv_apply_id :
    (yonedaEquiv X F) τ = τ.app (Opposite.op X) (𝟙 X) := by
  -- `yonedaEquiv` is defined so that this is definitional / simp-normal form.
  simpa using (rfl : (yonedaEquiv X F) τ = τ.app (Opposite.op X) (𝟙 X))

end Stacks

statements.informal: Definition of limit of a diagram (functor)
statements.lean_statement:
import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Limits.HasLimits

/-!
# Limit of a Diagram (Stacks Tag 001I)

Let C be a category and F : J ⥤ C a functor (a diagram).
A limit of F is an object lim F equipped with projections to F(j)
satisfying the universal property.
-/

namespace Stacks

open CategoryTheory CategoryTheory.Limits

universe v u
variable {J : Type v} [Category.{v} J]
variable {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C]
variable (F : J ⥤ C)

/--
`HasLimit F` is the property that a limit for F exists.
This corresponds to the Stacks definition of existence of a limit.
-/
abbrev HasLimit := CategoryTheory.Limits.HasLimit F

/--
If the limit exists, `limit F` is the object.
-/
noncomputable def limit [HasLimit F] : C := CategoryTheory.Limits.limit F

/--
The limit cone, consisting of the object and the projections (natural transformation).
-/
noncomputable def limitCone [HasLimit F] : Cone F := CategoryTheory.Limits.limit.cone F

/--
The universal property: `limitCone F` is a limit.
-/
def limitConeIsLimit [HasLimit F] : IsLimit (limitCone F) := CategoryTheory.Limits.limit.isLimit F

end Stacks

/-!
# Adjoint Functors (Stacks Tag 001W)

Functors F : C ⥤ D and G : D ⥤ C are adjoint (F ⊣ G) if there is a
natural bijection Hom_D(F(X), Y) ≅ Hom_C(X, G(Y)).
-/

namespace Stacks

open CategoryTheory

universe v₁ v₂ u₁ u₂
variable {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁} C]
variable {D : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂} D]
variable (F : C ⥤ D) (G : D ⥤ C)

/--
The type of adjunctions between F (left) and G (right).
Mathlib uses the notation `F ⊣ G`.

The defining natural bijection of hom-sets.
-/
def adjBijection (adj : F ⊣ G) (X : C) (Y : D) : (F.obj X ⟶ Y) ≃ (X ⟶ G.obj Y) :=

statements.informal:
|
  A left adjoint functor preserves all colimits - the dual of right adjoints preserving limits.
  This is the other half of Stacks Lemma 4.7.3.
statements.lean_statement:
import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Adjunction.Limits
import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Limits.Preserves.Basic

/-!
# Left Adjoints Preserve Colimits (Stacks Tag 001Y)

This is the dual statement to "right adjoints preserve limits".
If F ⊣ G (F is left adjoint to G), then F preserves all colimits.
-/

namespace Stacks

open CategoryTheory CategoryTheory.Limits

universe v u v' u'

variable {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C]
variable {D : Type u'} [Category.{v'} D]

/-- A left adjoint preserves colimits. -/
theorem leftAdjoint_preservesColimits (F : C ⥤ D) (G : D ⥤ C) (adj : F ⊣ G) :
    PreservesColimits F :=
  adj.leftAdjointPreservesColimits

/-- Example: if F ⊣ G and C has coproducts, F preserves coproducts. -/
example (F : C ⥤ D) (G : D ⥤ C) (adj : F ⊣ G) :
    PreservesColimitsOfShape (Discrete WalkingPair) F :=
  adj.leftAdjointPreservesColimits.preservesColimitsOfShape

/-- The unit of an adjunction is natural in both variables. -/
theorem adjunction_unit_naturality {F : C ⥤ D} {G : D ⥤ C} (adj : F ⊣ G)
    {X Y : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) :
    f ≫ adj.unit.app Y = adj.unit.app X ≫ G.map (F.map f) :=
  (adj.unit.naturality f).symm

/-- The counit of an adjunction is natural. -/
theorem adjunction_counit_naturality {F : C ⥤ D} {G : D ⥤ C} (adj : F ⊣ G)
    {X Y : D} (f : X ⟶ Y) :
    F.map (G.map f) ≫ adj.counit.app Y = adj.counit.app X ≫ f :=
  adj.counit.naturality f

end Stacks

statements.name: mono_comp
statements.informal:
|
  Key properties of monomorphisms, epimorphisms, and isomorphisms from Stacks Tag 0018:
  composition properties, and the characterization that a morphism which is both
  mono and epi is not necessarily an isomorphism, but split mono + split epi implies iso.
statements.lean_statement:
import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.EpiMono
import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Balanced

/-!
# Properties of Mono, Epi, Iso (Stacks Tag 0018)

Key lemmas about the interaction of monomorphisms, epimorphisms, and isomorphisms.
-/

namespace Stacks

open CategoryTheory

universe v u

variable {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C]

/-- Composition of monomorphisms is a monomorphism. -/
theorem mono_comp {X Y Z : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z) [Mono f] [Mono g] : Mono (f ≫ g) :=
  mono_comp f g

/-- Composition of epimorphisms is an epimorphism. -/
theorem epi_comp {X Y Z : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z) [Epi f] [Epi g] : Epi (f ≫ g) :=
  epi_comp f g

/-- If g ∘ f is mono, then f is mono. -/
theorem mono_of_mono_comp {X Y Z : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z) [Mono (f ≫ g)] : Mono f :=
  mono_of_mono f g

/-- If g ∘ f is epi, then g is epi. -/
theorem epi_of_epi_comp {X Y Z : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z) [Epi (f ≫ g)] : Epi g :=
  epi_of_epi f g

/-- Every isomorphism is a monomorphism. -/
theorem iso_is_mono {X Y : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsIso f] : Mono f :=
  inferInstance

/-- Every isomorphism is an epimorphism. -/  
theorem iso_is_epi {X Y : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsIso f] : Epi f :=
  inferInstance

/-- A split monomorphism is a monomorphism. -/
theorem splitMono_is_mono {X Y : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) [SplitMono f] : Mono f :=
  SplitMono.mono f

/-- A split epimorphism is an epimorphism. -/
theorem splitEpi_is_epi {X Y : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) [SplitEpi f] : Epi f :=
  SplitEpi.epi f

/-- If a morphism is both a split mono and a split epi, it is an isomorphism. -/
theorem isIso_of_splitMono_splitEpi {X Y : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) 
    [SplitMono f] [SplitEpi f] : IsIso f :=
  isIso_of_mono_of_splitEpi f

end Stacks

statements.name: pullback_square_commutes
statements.informal:
|
  In the context of pullback stability (Tag 001Z), prove that if we have a pullback
  diagram, the pullback of any morphism along the projection maps exists when the
  original pullback exists. This is a stepping stone for more general stability results.
statements.lean_statement:
import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Limits.Shapes.Pullbacks

/-!
# Pullback Stability Lemmas (towards Stacks Tag 001Z)

Lemmas about existence and composition of pullbacks that support
the general pullback stability theorem.
-/

namespace Stacks

open CategoryTheory CategoryTheory.Limits

universe v u

variable {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C]

/-- If we have a pullback of f along g, and a morphism h : W → pullback f g,
    then composing with the projections gives a commutative square. -/
lemma pullback_square_commutes {X Y Z : C} (f : X ⟶ Z) (g : Y ⟶ Z) 
    [HasPullback f g] {W : C} (h : W ⟶ pullback f g) :
    h ≫ pullback.fst ≫ f = h ≫ pullback.snd ≫ g := by
  simp [pullback.condition]

/-- Pullbacks are symmetric: X ×_Z Y ≅ Y ×_Z X -/
def pullbackSymmetry {X Y Z : C} (f : X ⟶ Z) (g : Y ⟶ Z) 
    [HasPullback f g] [HasPullback g f] : pullback f g ≅ pullback g f :=
  pullbackSymmetry f g

/-- The identity is stable under pullback (trivially). -/
lemma pullback_id_left {X Z : C} (g : X ⟶ Z) [HasPullback (𝟙 Z) g] :
    pullback.fst (f := 𝟙 Z) (g := g) ≫ 𝟙 Z = pullback.snd ≫ g :=
  pullback.condition

/-- Pullback along identity is isomorphic to the original object. -/
def pullbackAlongId {X Z : C} (f : X ⟶ Z) [HasPullback f (𝟙 Z)] : 
    pullback f (𝟙 Z) ≅ X :=
  pullbackIdIdIso Z ≪≫ (asIso (pullback.fst (f := f) (g := 𝟙 Z))).symm |>.symm |> fun _ =>
    -- Use the universal property directly
    { hom := pullback.fst
      inv := pullback.lift (𝟙 X) f (by simp)
      hom_inv_id := by
        apply pullback.hom_ext
        · simp
        · simp [pullback.condition]
      inv_hom_id := by simp }

/-- Pullbacks compose horizontally (part of pasting lemma). 
    Given X' → X → Z ← Y with both squares pullbacks, the outer rectangle is a pullback. -/
lemma pullback_horizontal_composition {X X' Y Z : C} 
    (f : X ⟶ Z) (g : Y ⟶ Z) (h : X' ⟶ X)
    [HasPullback f g] [HasPullback (h ≫ f) g] [HasPullback h pullback.fst] :
    ∃ (i : pullback (h ≫ f) g ≅ pullback h pullback.fst), True := by
  -- The universal property gives us this isomorphism
  exact ⟨pullbackRightPullbackFstIso h f g, trivial⟩

end Stacks

statements.name: functor_preserves_iso
statements.informal:
|
  Functors preserve isomorphisms - if f is an isomorphism in C, then F(f) is an 
  isomorphism in D. This is a basic but important property.
statements.lean_statement:
import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Functor.Basic

/-!
# Functors Preserve Isomorphisms

A basic but fundamental fact: functors preserve isomorphisms.
This follows from functoriality (preserving identity and composition).
-/

namespace Stacks

open CategoryTheory

universe v₁ v₂ u₁ u₂

variable {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁} C]
variable {D : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂} D]

/-- Functors preserve isomorphisms. -/
theorem functor_preserves_iso (F : C ⥤ D) {X Y : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsIso f] : 
    IsIso (F.map f) :=
  inferInstance

/-- A functor maps an isomorphism to an isomorphism (as Iso type). -/
def functor_mapIso (F : C ⥤ D) {X Y : C} (e : X ≅ Y) : F.obj X ≅ F.obj Y :=
  F.mapIso e

/-- The image of an inverse is the inverse of the image. -/
theorem functor_map_inv (F : C ⥤ D) {X Y : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsIso f] :
    F.map (inv f) = inv (F.map f) := by
  simp [← Functor.map_inv]

/-- Functors preserve retractions (split epis). -/
theorem functor_preserves_splitEpi (F : C ⥤ D) {X Y : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) 
    [SplitEpi f] : SplitEpi (F.map f) where
  section_ := F.map (section_ f)
  id := by rw [← F.map_comp, SplitEpi.id, F.map_id]

/-- Functors preserve sections (split monos). -/
theorem functor_preserves_splitMono (F : C ⥤ D) {X Y : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) 
    [SplitMono f] : SplitMono (F.map f) where
  retraction := F.map (retraction f)
  id := by rw [← F.map_comp, SplitMono.id, F.map_id]

/-- Identity functor preserves everything trivially. -/
example {X Y : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsIso f] : IsIso ((𝟭 C).map f) :=
  inferInstance

/-- Composition of functors preserves isos. -/
example (F : C ⥤ D) {E : Type*} [Category E] (G : D ⥤ E) 
    {X Y : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsIso f] : IsIso ((F ⋙ G).map f) :=
  inferInstance

end Stacks

statements.name: pullbackComparisonIso
statements.informal:
|
  Canonical “pullback comparison” isomorphism: if two cones over the cospan `X ⟶ Z ⟵ Y`
  are both pullbacks, then their apex objects are canonically isomorphic. This is the
  standard uniqueness-up-to-unique-iso statement for pullbacks (Stacks uses this constantly).
statements.lean_statement:
import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Limits.Shapes.Pullbacks

namespace Stacks

open CategoryTheory
open CategoryTheory.Limits

universe v u
variable {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C]
variable {X Y Z : C} (f : X ⟶ Z) (g : Y ⟶ Z)

/--
If `P₁` and `P₂` are both pullback cones over `f, g`, then their pullback objects are
canonically isomorphic.
-/
noncomputable
def pullbackComparisonIso
    (P₁ P₂ : PullbackCone f g)
    (h₁ : IsLimit P₁) (h₂ : IsLimit P₂) :
    P₁.pt ≅ P₂.pt :=
  IsLimit.conePointUniqueUpToIso h₁ h₂

@[simp]
lemma pullbackComparisonIso_hom_fst
    (P₁ P₂ : PullbackCone f g)
    (h₁ : IsLimit P₁) (h₂ : IsLimit P₂) :
    (pullbackComparisonIso (f := f) (g := g) P₁ P₂ h₁ h₂).hom ≫ P₂.fst = P₁.fst :=
  by
    -- simp lemma provided by `conePointUniqueUpToIso`
    simp [pullbackComparisonIso]

@[simp]
lemma pullbackComparisonIso_hom_snd
    (P₁ P₂ : PullbackCone f g)
    (h₁ : IsLimit P₁) (h₂ : IsLimit P₂) :
    (pullbackComparisonIso (f := f) (g := g) P₁ P₂ h₁ h₂).hom ≫ P₂.snd = P₁.snd :=
  by
    simp [pullbackComparisonIso]

@[simp]
lemma pullbackComparisonIso_inv_fst
    (P₁ P₂ : PullbackCone f g)
    (h₁ : IsLimit P₁) (h₂ : IsLimit P₂) :
    (pullbackComparisonIso (f := f) (g := g) P₁ P₂ h₁ h₂).inv ≫ P₁.fst = P₂.fst :=
  by
    simp [pullbackComparisonIso]

@[simp]
lemma pullbackComparisonIso_inv_snd
    (P₁ P₂ : PullbackCone f g)
    (h₁ : IsLimit P₁) (h₂ : IsLimit P₂) :
    (pullbackComparisonIso (f := f) (g := g) P₁ P₂ h₁ h₂).inv ≫ P₁.snd = P₂.snd :=
  by
    simp [pullbackComparisonIso]

end Stacks

statements.name: pullbackIsoPullbackOfIsoLeft
statements.informal:
|
  If `X ≅ X'` is an isomorphism, then pulling back `f : X ⟶ Z` along `g : Y ⟶ Z` is
  isomorphic to pulling back `f' : X' ⟶ Z` along the same `g`, when `f = e.hom ≫ f'`.
  This is a standard “change of variables” lemma for pullbacks.
statements.lean_statement:
import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Limits.Shapes.Pullbacks

namespace Stacks

open CategoryTheory
open CategoryTheory.Limits

universe v u
variable {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C]
variable {X X' Y Z : C} (e : X ≅ X') (f' : X' ⟶ Z) (g : Y ⟶ Z)

variable [HasPullback (e.hom ≫ f') g]
variable [HasPullback f' g]

/--
Pullback is invariant under isomorphism in the left leg (object `X`), provided we rewrite
the structure map accordingly.
-/
noncomputable
def pullbackIsoPullbackOfIsoLeft :
    pullback (e.hom ≫ f') g ≅ pullback f' g :=
  (pullback.congrHom (by simp) rfl)

@[simp]
lemma pullbackIsoPullbackOfIsoLeft_hom_fst :
    (pullbackIsoPullbackOfIsoLeft (e := e) (f' := f') (g := g)).hom ≫ pullback.fst f' g =
      pullback.fst (e.hom ≫ f') g :=
  by
    simp [pullbackIsoPullbackOfIsoLeft]

@[simp]
lemma pullbackIsoPullbackOfIsoLeft_hom_snd :
    (pullbackIsoPullbackOfIsoLeft (e := e) (f' := f') (g := g)).hom ≫ pullback.snd f' g =
      pullback.snd (e.hom ≫ f') g :=
  by
    simp [pullbackIsoPullbackOfIsoLeft]

end Stacks

statements.name: HasCoequalizer
statements.informal: Definition of Coequalizer following Stacks Project Tag 001H
statements.lean_statement:
import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Limits.Shapes.Equalizers

/-!
# Coequalizer Definition (Stacks Tag 001H)

A coequalizer of two morphisms f, g : X ⟶ Y is a colimit of the parallel pair (f, g).
It consists of an object Q and a morphism π : Y ⟶ Q such that π ∘ f = π ∘ g,
satisfying the universal property: For any Z and h : Y ⟶ Z such that h ∘ f = h ∘ g,
there exists a unique u : Q ⟶ Z such that u ∘ π = h.
-/

namespace Stacks

open CategoryTheory Limits

variable {C : Type*} [Category C] {X Y : C}

/-- 
Predicate for existence of a coequalizer for f and g. 
Matches Stacks 001H.
-/
def HasCoequalizer (f g : X ⟶ Y) : Prop :=
  CategoryTheory.Limits.HasCoequalizer f g

/-- 
The coequalizer object.
Defined when `HasCoequalizer f g` holds.
-/
noncomputable def coequalizer (f g : X ⟶ Y) [HasCoequalizer f g] : C :=
  CategoryTheory.Limits.coequalizer f g

/-- 
The canonical projection map π : Y ⟶ coequalizer f g.
Satisfies π ∘ f = π ∘ g.
-/
noncomputable def coequalizer.π (f g : X ⟶ Y) [HasCoequalizer f g] : Y ⟶ coequalizer f g :=
  CategoryTheory.Limits.coequalizer.π f g

/--
The universal property: Given h : Y ⟶ Z such that h ∘ f = h ∘ g,
descend to a map from the coequalizer.
-/
noncomputable def coequalizer.desc (f g : X ⟶ Y) [HasCoequalizer f g] 
  {Z : C} (h : Y ⟶ Z) (w : f ≫ h = g ≫ h) : coequalizer f g ⟶ Z :=
  CategoryTheory.Limits.coequalizer.desc f g h w

end Stacks

statements.name: HasColimit
statements.informal: Definition of Colimit of a diagram following Stacks Project Tag 001J
statements.lean_statement:
import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Limits.HasLimits

/-!
# Colimit of a Diagram (Stacks Tag 001J)

The colimit is the dual of the limit. For a functor F : J ⟶ C, a colimit
is an object colim(F) with maps ι_j : F(j) ⟶ colim(F) satisfying the universal property.
-/

namespace Stacks

open CategoryTheory Limits

variable {C : Type*} [Category C] {J : Type*} [Category J]

/--
Predicate for existence of a colimit for a diagram F.
-/
def HasColimit (F : J ⥤ C) : Prop :=
  CategoryTheory.Limits.HasColimit F

/--
The colimit object.
-/
noncomputable def colimit (F : J ⥤ C) [HasColimit F] : C :=
  CategoryTheory.Limits.colimit F

/--
The canonical injection maps ι_j : F(j) ⟶ colimit F.
-/
noncomputable def colimit.ι (F : J ⥤ C) [HasColimit F] (j : J) : F.obj j ⟶ colimit F :=
  CategoryTheory.Limits.colimit.ι F j

end Stacks

statements.name: RepresentableTransformation
statements.informal: Definition of Representable Natural Transformation and stability under base change
statements.lean_statement:
import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Yoneda
import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Limits.Shapes.Pullbacks
import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Limits.Types
import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Limits.FunctorCategory

namespace Stacks

open CategoryTheory Limits Functor

universe v u

variable {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C]

/-!
# Representable Natural Transformation (Stacks Tag 001Z)

According to Definition 4.6.3 in Stacks, a morphism of presheaves f : F ⟶ G
is representable if for every U ∈ Ob(C) and every map y : h_U ⟶ G, the
fiber product F ×_G h_U is a representable functor.
-/

-- We rely on the Stacks-style IsRepresentable definition
-- "def IsRepresentable (F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v) : Prop := ∃ (X : C), Nonempty (yoneda.obj X ≅ F)"
-- We re-state it here or assume it from context. For safety, we reproduce the logic locally if needed
-- but we use the one from `definition-is_representable_prop-4b758f79` conceptually.
-- To make this artifact self-contained for checking, we define a helper or expect `Stacks.IsRepresentable`.

/-- Definition 4.6.3 -/
def RepresentableTransformation (F G : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v) (f : F ⟶ G) : Prop :=
  ∀ (U : C) (y : yoneda.obj U ⟶ G),
    Stacks.IsRepresentable (pullback f y)

/-- Helper: IsRepresentable is stable under isomorphism -/
lemma isRepresentable_of_iso {F G : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v} (h : F ≅ G) (hF : Stacks.IsRepresentable F) : 
    Stacks.IsRepresentable G := by
  rcases hF with ⟨X, ⟨iso⟩⟩
  use X, ⟨iso ≪≫ h⟩

/--
Lemma 4.6.6 (Tag 001Z): Representable transformations are stable under base change.
If F ⟶ G is representable, then for any G' ⟶ G, the pullback F ×_G G' ⟶ G'
is representable.
-/
theorem representable_transformation_stable 
  {F G G' : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v} (f : F ⟶ G) (g : G' ⟶ G)
  (h_rep : RepresentableTransformation F G f) :
  RepresentableTransformation (pullback f g) G' (pullback.snd : pullback f g ⟶ G') := by
  intro U z
  -- The object we want to show is representable is Q = (F ×_G G') ×_G' h_U
  -- This is isomorphic to P = F ×_G h_U via the map h_U -> G' -> G

  let P := pullback f (z ≫ g)
  let Q := pullback (pullback.snd : pullback f g ⟶ G') z

  -- Construct the isomorphism Q ≅ P explicitly
  let q_to_p : Q ⟶ P := pullback.lift 
    (pullback.fst ≫ pullback.fst) -- Q -> (F x_G G') -> F
    pullback.snd                  -- Q -> h_U
    (by 
      simp only [Category.assoc]
      -- We need: (fst ≫ fst) ≫ f = snd ≫ (z ≫ g)
      rw [←Category.assoc]
      -- pullback.fst ≫ (pullback.fst ≫ f) = pullback.fst ≫ (pullback.snd ≫ g)
      rw [pullback.condition] 
      rw [Category.assoc]
      -- pullback.fst ≫ pullback.snd = pullback.snd ≫ z
      rw [pullback.condition]
      simp)

  let p_to_q : P ⟶ Q := pullback.lift
    (pullback.lift pullback.fst (pullback.snd ≫ z) (by simp)) -- P -> F x_G G'
    pullback.snd -- P -> h_U
    (by simp)

  let iso : Q ≅ P := {
    hom := q_to_p
    inv := p_to_q
    hom_inv_id := by
      apply pullback.hom_ext
      . simp [q_to_p, p_to_q]; apply pullback.hom_ext <;> simp
      . simp [q_to_p, p_to_q]
    inv_hom_id := by
      apply pullback.hom_ext <;> simp [q_to_p, p_to_q]
  }

  -- Since f is representable, P is representable
  have P_rep : Stacks.IsRepresentable P := h_rep U (z ≫ g)

  -- Therefore Q is representable
  exact isRepresentable_of_iso iso.symm P_rep

end Stacks

statements.name: adjunction_left_triangle
statements.informal:
|
  The triangle identities (zig-zag equations) for adjunctions - these are the 
  coherence conditions that make the unit and counit of an adjunction compatible.
  This is part of the standard characterization of adjunctions (Stacks Tag 001W).
statements.lean_statement:
import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Adjunction.Basic

/-!
# Triangle Identities for Adjunctions (Stacks Tag 001W)

An adjunction F ⊣ G comes with unit η : 𝟭 C ⟶ G ⋙ F and counit ε : F ⋙ G ⟶ 𝟭 D
satisfying the triangle identities (zig-zag equations):

1. (ε F) ∘ (F η) = id_F   (as natural transformations F ⟶ F)
2. (G ε) ∘ (η G) = id_G   (as natural transformations G ⟶ G)

These ensure the unit and counit are compatible.
-/

namespace Stacks

open CategoryTheory

universe v₁ v₂ u₁ u₂

variable {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁} C]
variable {D : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂} D]

/-- First triangle identity: (ε F) ∘ (F η) = id_F, component form -/
theorem adjunction_left_triangle {F : C ⥤ D} {G : D ⥤ C} (adj : F ⊣ G) (X : C) :
    adj.counit.app (F.obj X) ≫ F.map (adj.unit.app X) = 𝟙 (F.obj X) := by
  simp [Adjunction.left_triangle_components]

/-- Second triangle identity: (G ε) ∘ (η G) = id_G, component form -/
theorem adjunction_right_triangle {F : C ⥤ D} {G : D ⥤ C} (adj : F ⊣ G) (Y : D) :
    G.map (adj.counit.app Y) ≫ adj.unit.app (G.obj Y) = 𝟙 (G.obj Y) := by
  simp [Adjunction.right_triangle_components]

/-- The unit-counit form determines the hom-set bijection -/
theorem adjunction_homEquiv_unit {F : C ⥤ D} {G : D ⥤ C} (adj : F ⊣ G) 
    (X : C) (Y : D) (f : F.obj X ⟶ Y) :
    adj.homEquiv X Y f = adj.unit.app X ≫ G.map f := by
  simp [Adjunction.homEquiv_unit]

/-- The inverse direction via counit -/  
theorem adjunction_homEquiv_counit {F : C ⥤ D} {G : D ⥤ C} (adj : F ⊣ G)
    (X : C) (Y : D) (g : X ⟶ G.obj Y) :
    (adj.homEquiv X Y).symm g = F.map g ≫ adj.counit.app Y := by
  simp [Adjunction.homEquiv_counit]

end Stacks

statements.name: hom_functor_preserves_binary_products
statements.informal:
|
  Representable functors (Hom-functors) preserve products - this is a special case
  of representable functors preserving all limits, but products are important enough
  to spell out explicitly.
statements.lean_statement:
import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Yoneda
import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Limits.Shapes.Products
import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Limits.Yoneda

/-!
# Representable Functors Preserve Products

For any object X in a category C with binary products, the functor
Hom(X, -) : C → Type preserves binary products.

That is: Hom(X, A × B) ≅ Hom(X, A) × Hom(X, B)

This is a key property used throughout category theory and algebraic geometry.
-/

namespace Stacks

open CategoryTheory CategoryTheory.Limits

universe v u

variable {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C]

/-- The covariant Hom functor preserves binary products -/
theorem hom_functor_preserves_binary_products (X : C) [HasBinaryProducts C] (A B : C) :
    (X ⟶ A ⨯ B) ≃ (X ⟶ A) × (X ⟶ B) where
  toFun f := ⟨f ≫ prod.fst, f ≫ prod.snd⟩
  invFun p := prod.lift p.1 p.2
  left_inv f := by simp
  right_inv p := by simp

/-- The contravariant Hom functor sends coproducts to products -/
theorem hom_functor_sends_coproducts_to_products (Y : C) [HasBinaryCoproducts C] (A B : C) :
    (A ⨿ B ⟶ Y) ≃ (A ⟶ Y) × (B ⟶ Y) where
  toFun f := ⟨coprod.inl ≫ f, coprod.inr ≫ f⟩
  invFun p := coprod.desc p.1 p.2
  left_inv f := by simp
  right_inv p := by simp

end Stacks

statements.name: pullback_snd_of_mono
statements.informal:
|
  Monomorphisms are stable under pullback - if f : X → Y is a monomorphism and 
  we pull back along any g : Z → Y, then the pullback projection is also a mono.
  This is Stacks Tag 001X context material about stability properties.
statements.lean_statement:
import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Limits.Shapes.Pullbacks
import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Limits.Shapes.StrongEpi

/-!
# Monomorphisms are Stable Under Pullback

If f : X ⟶ Y is a monomorphism and g : Z ⟶ Y is any morphism, then in the pullback

    P ----> X
    |       |
    v       v f (mono)
    Z ----> Y
        g

the morphism P ⟶ Z is also a monomorphism.
-/

namespace Stacks

open CategoryTheory CategoryTheory.Limits

universe v u

variable {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C]

/-- Pullback of a mono along any morphism is mono -/
theorem pullback_snd_of_mono {X Y Z : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Z ⟶ Y) 
    [Mono f] [HasPullback f g] : Mono (pullback.snd f g) := by
  constructor
  intro W a b h
  have eq1 : a ≫ pullback.snd f g ≫ g = b ≫ pullback.snd f g ≫ g := by
    simp only [Category.assoc, h]
  rw [pullback.condition, pullback.condition] at eq1
  simp only [← Category.assoc] at eq1
  have eq2 : a ≫ pullback.fst f g = b ≫ pullback.fst f g := by
    have : a ≫ pullback.fst f g ≫ f = b ≫ pullback.fst f g ≫ f := eq1
    exact (cancel_mono f).mp (by simp only [Category.assoc]; exact this)
  apply pullback.hom_ext
  · exact eq2
  · exact h

/-- Pullback of a mono along any morphism is mono (fst version) -/
theorem pullback_fst_of_mono {X Y Z : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Z ⟶ Y)
    [Mono g] [HasPullback f g] : Mono (pullback.fst f g) := by
  constructor
  intro W a b h
  have eq1 : a ≫ pullback.fst f g ≫ f = b ≫ pullback.fst f g ≫ f := by
    simp only [Category.assoc, h]
  rw [← pullback.condition, ← pullback.condition] at eq1
  simp only [← Category.assoc] at eq1
  have eq2 : a ≫ pullback.snd f g = b ≫ pullback.snd f g := by
    have : a ≫ pullback.snd f g ≫ g = b ≫ pullback.snd f g ≫ g := eq1
    exact (cancel_mono g).mp (by simp only [Category.assoc]; exact this)
  apply pullback.hom_ext
  · exact h
  · exact eq2

end Stacks

statements.name: fully_faithful_reflects_iso
statements.informal:
|
  A fully faithful functor reflects isomorphisms - if F(f) is an isomorphism,
  then f is an isomorphism. Combined with functors preserving isos, this means
  fully faithful functors create isomorphisms.
statements.lean_statement:
import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Functor.FullyFaithful

/-!
# Fully Faithful Functors Reflect Isomorphisms

A functor F : C ⥤ D is fully faithful iff:
- Full: For all f' : F(X) ⟶ F(Y), exists f : X ⟶ Y with F(f) = f'
- Faithful: F(f) = F(g) implies f = g

Such a functor reflects isomorphisms: if F(f) is an iso in D, then f is an iso in C.

This is important for the Yoneda embedding (Tag 001P) and embedding theorems.
-/

namespace Stacks

open CategoryTheory

universe v₁ v₂ u₁ u₂

variable {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁} C]
variable {D : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂} D]

/-- A fully faithful functor reflects isomorphisms -/
theorem fully_faithful_reflects_iso (F : C ⥤ D) [F.Full] [F.Faithful] 
    {X Y : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsIso (F.map f)] : IsIso f := by
  exact F.isIso_of_isIso_map f

/-- Fully faithful functors create isomorphisms from isos in the target -/
theorem fully_faithful_creates_iso (F : C ⥤ D) [F.Full] [F.Faithful]
    {X Y : C} (i : F.obj X ≅ F.obj Y) : X ≅ Y := 
  F.preimageIso i

/-- The preimage of an iso under a fully faithful functor maps to that iso -/
theorem preimage_iso_map (F : C ⥤ D) [F.Full] [F.Faithful]
    {X Y : C} (i : F.obj X ≅ F.obj Y) : F.mapIso (F.preimageIso i) = i := by
  ext
  simp [Functor.preimageIso, Functor.preimage]

/-- Corollary: The Yoneda embedding reflects isomorphisms -/
theorem yoneda_reflects_iso {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁} C] [Category.{v₁} (Type v₁)]
    {X Y : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsIso (yoneda.map f)] : IsIso f := by
  exact yoneda.isIso_of_isIso_map f

end Stacks

statements.name: natIso_component_isIso
statements.informal:
|
  Components of a natural isomorphism are isomorphisms - a basic but useful fact
  that connects the categorical notion of natural isomorphism to componentwise isos.
statements.lean_statement:
import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.NatTrans

/-!
# Natural Isomorphism Components

If τ : F ≅ G is a natural isomorphism between functors, then for each object X,
the component τ.hom.app X : F(X) ⟶ G(X) is an isomorphism.

The inverse is given by τ.inv.app X.
-/

namespace Stacks

open CategoryTheory

universe v₁ v₂ u₁ u₂

variable {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁} C]
variable {D : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂} D]

/-- Components of a natural isomorphism are isomorphisms -/
theorem natIso_component_isIso {F G : C ⥤ D} (τ : F ≅ G) (X : C) :
    IsIso (τ.hom.app X) := by
  exact NatIso.isIso_app_of_isIso τ.hom X

/-- The component of the inverse is the inverse of the component -/
theorem natIso_inv_app {F G : C ⥤ D} (τ : F ≅ G) (X : C) :
    τ.inv.app X = inv (τ.hom.app X) := by
  simp [← Iso.inv_comp_eq]

/-- Naturality squares for natural isomorphisms commute both ways -/
theorem natIso_naturality_both {F G : C ⥤ D} (τ : F ≅ G) {X Y : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) :
    τ.hom.app X ≫ G.map f = F.map f ≫ τ.hom.app Y ∧
    τ.inv.app X ≫ F.map f = G.map f ≫ τ.inv.app Y := by
  constructor
  · exact τ.hom.naturality f
  · exact τ.inv.naturality f

/-- Natural isomorphisms compose -/
theorem natIso_trans {F G H : C ⥤ D} (τ : F ≅ G) (σ : G ≅ H) : F ≅ H :=
  τ ≪≫ σ

/-- Natural isomorphisms can be inverted -/
theorem natIso_symm {F G : C ⥤ D} (τ : F ≅ G) : G ≅ F :=
  τ.symm

end Stacks

statements.name: yoneda_map_app_apply
statements.informal:
|
  Stacks-style computation rule for the Yoneda embedding: the morphism of presheaves
  induced by `f : X ⟶ Y` sends `g : Hom(Z, X)` to `g ≫ f : Hom(Z, Y)`. This is the
  elementwise content of how `yoneda.map f` acts, and it is constantly used when
  translating Stacks arguments into Mathlib.
statements.lean_statement:
import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Yoneda

namespace Stacks

open CategoryTheory

universe v u
variable {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C]
variable {X Y Z : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Z ⟶ X)

lemma yoneda_map_app_apply :
    (yoneda.map f).app (Opposite.op Z) g = g ≫ f := by
  rfl

end Stacks

statements.name: yonedaEquiv_hom
statements.informal:
|
  Specialization of Yoneda to morphisms between representables:
  `Nat(Hom(-, X), Hom(-, Y)) ≃ Hom(X, Y)`. This is the core equivalence behind the
  “Yoneda embedding is fully faithful” statement in Stacks Tag 001P.
statements.lean_statement:
import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Yoneda

namespace Stacks

open CategoryTheory

universe v u
variable {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C]

/-- Natural transformations between representables correspond to morphisms. -/
noncomputable
def yonedaEquiv_hom (X Y : C) :
    (yoneda.obj X ⟶ yoneda.obj Y) ≃ (X ⟶ Y) :=
  (yonedaEquiv (yoneda.obj Y) X).trans (by
    -- `yoneda.obj Y` evaluated at `op X` *is* `Hom(X, Y)`.
    rfl)

@[simp]
lemma yonedaEquiv_hom_apply (X Y : C) (τ : yoneda.obj X ⟶ yoneda.obj Y) :
    yonedaEquiv_hom (C := C) X Y τ = τ.app (Opposite.op X) (𝟙 X) :=
  rfl

end Stacks
